title: Embracing the future of Artificial Intelligence in the classroom: the relevance of AI literacy, prompt engineering, and critical thinking in modern education
venue: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education
extended_summary:
This paper discusses the growing role of artificial intelligence in education, with a particular emphasis on AI literacy, prompt engineering, and critical thinking. Rather than evaluating a specific educational intervention with outcome data, it argues that these three competencies are increasingly necessary for responsible and effective AI use in academic settings. The author frames AI as both an opportunity for personalized learning and a challenge because of issues such as hallucinations, misuse, overreliance, and inadequate educator preparation.

The paper combines a case study from Kalaidos University of Applied Sciences in Zurich, Switzerland, with a narrative literature review. The case study describes institutional responses to the sudden spread of ChatGPT and other large language models, including the development of internal AI guidelines for student writing. These guidelines require transparency about model use, documentation of how AI was used, and critical evaluation of outputs. The discussion then broadens to suggest workshops, curriculum integration, and institutional support structures to build a stronger AI culture among students, teachers, and administrators.

The paper concludes that simple rules or bans are insufficient and that effective integration of AI into education requires systematic training and ongoing support. It argues that AI literacy should include technical understanding, awareness of limitations and ethics, and practical use cases; prompt engineering should be taught as a pedagogical skill; and critical thinking should remain central so that students do not treat AI as a substitute for independent work. The overall contribution is conceptual and practice-oriented, focused on higher education rather than a controlled empirical evaluation.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual discussion with a narrative literature review and informal case observations, not a controlled empirical study. It does not present a clear experimental or quasi-experimental methodology for causal inference.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports no measurable educational impact on student achievement or other outcomes. Its contributions are normative and practical suggestions rather than evidence of observed impact.

interventions.use_case: Conceptual discussion of ChatGPT and similar large language models as classroom support tools, including using them as an 'informed conversational partner' for student academic work and as a sparring partner for brainstorming, drafting, and questioning.
AI literacy instruction and prompt engineering pedagogy, including workshops, AI-literacy courses, and guided practice in how to interact with AI systems responsibly and critically.

finding.finding_summary: The paper argues that AI literacy, prompt engineering, and critical thinking are essential durable skills for students in AI-rich educational settings. It does not report an empirical effect estimate; instead, it provides a conceptual and case-based rationale that structured AI use can strengthen students' critical evaluation of AI outputs and problem-solving capacity.
finding.measure: Conceptual synthesis and case-study-informed discussion of AI literacy, prompt engineering, and critical thinking

finding.finding_summary: The paper proposes institutional AI guidelines, staff workshops, dedicated budgets, and paid AI-support roles as strategies for integrating AI into higher education. No quantitative institutional outcome is reported, but the central claim is that governance and training structures are needed to manage AI use responsibly and consistently.
finding.measure: Policy and governance recommendations derived from a university case study

finding.finding_summary: The article suggests that AI tools can improve efficiency for tasks such as curriculum design, case-study creation, and brainstorming for academic writing. These claims are illustrative rather than measured, and no effect sizes or sample-based comparisons are provided.
finding.measure: Narrative descriptions of teacher workflow support and content-generation efficiency
